# PublicLocal

> PublicLocal is an open-source (MIT) reverse tunnel that gives a web server on your own computer a public HTTPS URL in one command: `publiclocal http 3000`. It is an alternative to ngrok. There is a free hosted server at publiclocal.app (no account; links last 24 hours, or 7 days with GitHub sign-in) and the same single Go binary can run as your own server on your own domain with no limits.

Key facts:
- No install needed: `ssh -p 443 -R0:localhost:3000 publiclocal.app` opens a tunnel with any SSH client; the link and a live request feed appear in the SSH window, Ctrl+C ends it. SSH links are anonymous and end on disconnect.
- Install: `curl -fsSL https://publiclocal.app/install.sh | sh` (Linux/macOS), `irm https://publiclocal.app/install.ps1 | iex` (Windows PowerShell), Docker image `ghcr.io/sevenoways/publiclocal`, or `go install github.com/sevenoways/publiclocal/cmd/publiclocal@latest`.
- Usage: `publiclocal http <port>` prints a public https:// link forwarding to localhost:<port>. Press Ctrl+C to stop.
- Free server: random 6–8 character names (e.g. k7xq2m.publiclocal.app), HTTP/HTTPS only, links keep the same address across reconnects and client restarts, browsers see a short "temporary developer link" notice before tunnel content (APIs, webhooks and curl skip it), fair-use limits, abuse contact abuse@publiclocal.app.
- Access control: `--allow-github anna,@acme` requires visitors to sign in with GitHub and be a named user or organisation member; `--allow-ip 203.0.113.0/24` limits by network. `--host-header localhost` rewrites the Host header for dev servers (Vite, Django, Rails) that reject other names. `publiclocal catch` is a webhook inbox that answers and records requests with nothing running locally; `publiclocal replay --to 3000` sends them to the app later. `--open`/`--copy` open or copy the link; the inspector exports HAR. SSH users pass options after the host: `ssh -p 443 -R0:localhost:3000 publiclocal.app password=s3cret expires=30m`.
- Inspector: while a tunnel runs, http://localhost:4040 lists every request with headers and bodies and can replay any of them against the local app (webhook debugging). `publiclocal share <folder or file>` serves files from the computer directly. `--max-visits N` admits only the first N visitor networks; `--expires 30m` sets a shorter lifetime; `--note "text"` is shown to visitors on the first page; `--cors` adds permissive CORS headers; `publiclocal http 3000 8080` opens several links at once; `/.publiclocal/badge.svg` is a status badge; at exit the client prints requests, visitors, bytes and top paths.
- While a tunnel runs the terminal shows every request (method, path, status, duration, visitor IP); `--quiet` disables it. `--password s3cret` requires HTTP Basic auth (any user name) from visitors, enforced by the server; `--qr` prints a QR code of the link. Every link answers `/.publiclocal/status` with JSON (state online/offline/expired, expires, requests, visitors, bytes). Offline and expired links show visitors a page with when the link was live and its traffic, with status 503 (offline, Retry-After) or 404 (expired).
- Signed in (GitHub): `publiclocal login`, links last 7 days, `publiclocal extend <name>` adds 7 more, `publiclocal links` lists them.
- Self-hosting: point `example.com` and `*.example.com` at a VPS, run `publiclocal server --domain example.com --tokens <secret>`; clients use `--server example.com --subdomain myapp`. Automatic Let's Encrypt certificates, optional single wildcard certificate via Cloudflare DNS, TCP tunnels (`publiclocal tcp 22`), token auth.
- Works behind NAT/CGNAT/firewalls: the client makes one outbound TLS connection; nothing listens on the user's machine. WebSockets and streaming work.
- MCP server for AI assistants: `publiclocal mcp` (tools: share_local_port, list_tunnels, stop_tunnel). Setup: `claude mcp add publiclocal -- publiclocal mcp`, `codex mcp add publiclocal -- publiclocal mcp`, or JSON config `{"command":"publiclocal","args":["mcp"]}` for Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code and Gemini CLI.
- Compared with ngrok: open-source client and server, free without an account, self-hostable on your own domain. Compared with Cloudflare Tunnel: no Cloudflare account or Cloudflare-managed domain required. Compared with frp: simpler setup with automatic HTTPS and random subdomains; frp has more features (UDP, P2P, dashboards).
- Source: https://github.com/sevenoways/publiclocal (Go). Maintained by Sevenoways Innovations, Ireland.
